confidence_notes: Restaurant and drink anchors draw on crowdsourced Expatistan and Numbeo figures and older Westword snapshots (2017 and 2022), so they are rough. Inexpensive meal (~$20/person) is the best-supported restaurant anchor. Cappuccino ($5.50) is cross-checked against Expatistan (~$6) and undated Toast menu listings ($3.75 to $5.50). Beer ($7.00) and cocktail ($15.00) are checked against Expatistan's Denver figures ($8 pub beer, $16 downtown cocktail) and 2022 Westword figures. No current Denver wine-by-the-glass figure was found, so wine_glass ($13.00) is a bounded estimate based on the beer and cocktail relationship and typical US restaurant pours; treat it as low confidence. The mid-range two-person meal ($130) is a holistic estimate, since the sources conflict ($88 in 2022 including wine, about $156 in Expatistan's expat-area estimate). All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season. No booking pages or current listings were inspected. FX: the 0.6955 observation for 15 October 2026 was reported in an RBA Exchange Rates Overview search summary. I did not read the RBA table directly, and a 7 to 9 October range was also reported. An earlier March 2026 RBA snapshot was stale and not used.
comparable_city_reasoning: Denver-specific crowdsourced restaurant and drink data where available, with US metro norms for wine and mid-range dining. Accommodation is a holistic estimate from general knowledge of Denver summer hotel and hostel rates.
